humanities_role_explanation: The benchmark targets LLM competence on cultural heritage knowledge and values (types, values, conservation, management, utilization), judged by heritage professionals against scholarly consensus; it is not generic QA using heritage text as material.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only single-turn queries about cultural heritage and LLM-generated text responses; multimodal and multi-turn settings are explicitly left unexplored.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Four question types: critical query (open-ended opinion/discussion), fact verification (including true/false), causal inference, and interpretation (explaining terms, events, objects). Model responses are classified into eight cultural value misalignment types (detail inaccuracy, cultural misunderstanding, knowledge gap, premature certainty, cultural reductionism, historical bias, selective narration, contextual irrelevance) via ChatGPT plus human experts.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Scoped to the cultural heritage domain and value misalignment in generated text.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: LLaMA-3-8B, Qwen-7B, Baichuan2-7B, Yi-6B, Mistral-7B evaluated; GPT-4o used as query generator and judge.

quantitative_metrics.note: Value misalignment rates (%) per aspect, model and misalignment type; Likert severity ratings.

summary: The paper introduces CHVM-1K, a set of 1066 cultural heritage queries organized in a 5-category, 17-aspect knowledge framework, and a workflow combining an LLM judge with heritage professionals to detect value misalignment in LLM responses. Evaluating five open-source LLMs, it finds over 65% of generated texts exhibit misalignment across eight identified types.
key_findings: Over 65% of generated texts show notable misalignment; rates range from 30.16% (A3, Yi-6B) to 92.42% (A6, LLaMA-3-8B). Contextual irrelevance (VM8) and detail inaccuracy (VM1) are the most frequent types; premature certainty (VM4) is the least. LLaMA-3-8B is worst, Mistral-7B slightly best. Heritage professionals rated VM1 as most severe.
facets_explanation: Queries were generated by ChatGPT from professional-selected keywords and refined by heritage professionals. Misalignment labels come from a GPT-4o judge with in-context examples, with about 30% high-confidence labels spot-checked and the remaining 70% labelled by heritage experts in a two-round process, with disagreements resolved by group consensus. Judging requires external scholarly knowledge not in the query. Labels are not matched against a single key but assigned by expert/LLM judgment, and disagreement is resolved to consensus.
results_explanation: The paper reports misalignment rates (lower is better) rather than a single headline score; ranges are 30.16% (A3, Yi-6B) to 92.42% (A6, LLaMA-3-8B), so reported_best_score is null. No human baseline or format comparison is reported. Cultural asymmetry across regions is not reported as a finding, though the limitations note the dataset focuses on Asian heritage.

humanities_role.quote: we systematically assess the reliability of LLMs in generating culturally aligned texts for cultural heritage-related tasks

dataset_size.quote: The dataset for cultural value misalignment detection contains 1066 query-response pairs

evaluation_set_size.quote: The dataset for cultural value misalignment detection contains 1066 query-response pairs

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: the evaluation presented in this study is conducted on general-purpose LLMs without fine tuning on domain specific data

gold_source.quote: a team of cultural heritage scholars and domain experts collaborates to further label these query-response pairs according to their misalignment types

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: its response, which divides the stages into six, contradicts the academic consensus

answer_multiplicity.quote: we assessed whether the LLM-generated responses contained value misalignments using an advanced LLM with a well-designed prompt

plurality_treatment.quote: In cases of disagreement, all evaluators participated in a group discussion to reach a final consensus.
